item.text: I’m checking the current implementation for the next real refactor boundary. At this size, the only worthwhile changes are ones that simplify the algorithm or sharpen the public contract without changing behavior.

I’m replacing the boxed `List<List<Float>>` bucket storage with primitive bucket arrays behind a small internal type. That keeps the public API the same but simplifies data flow and removes the repeated boxing/unboxing in the hot path.
I’ve applied the storage refactor. I’m extending the test harness slightly so the public API contract is clearer, especially around `sortedCopy(...)` returning a separate array instance.
The test contract is updated. I’m compiling and running the demo plus the tests now to verify the primitive-bucket refactor didn’t change behavior.

Refactored the core implementation in [BucketSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSort.java:1) to use primitive bucket storage instead of `List<List<Float>>`. The public API is unchanged, but the internal flow is cleaner now: values are validated once, distributed into a small internal `Buckets` type, sorted bucket-by-bucket with primitive arrays, then written back with `System.arraycopy(...)`. That removes the boxing/unboxing overhead and makes the algorithm easier to reason about.

I also tightened [BucketSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSortTest.java:1) with an explicit check that `sortedCopy(...)` returns a distinct array instance, so the non-mutating contract is verified directly.
